findings.title: Early `return true` on `dateOverrideExist` skips busy-time check, allowing double bookings on override dates
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a slot falls within a date override, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately return `true` before reaching `busy.every(...)` at line 153. As a result, existing Cal bookings and external calendar busy times are completely ignored on any day that has a date override, causing already-booked slots to be shown as available and allowing double-booking.

findings.title: Comparing two Dayjs objects with `===` is always false, breaking full-day unavailable overrides
findings.body: Line 114 checks `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` to detect a 0-length (unavailable all day) date override. Because `dayjs(...)` returns a new object instance each time, `===` compares object references and always evaluates to `false`. Use `.isSame(...)` instead (or compare `date.start.getTime() === date.end.getTime()`).

findings.title: Boundary conditions in date override check allow slots that only partially overlap or start at override end
findings.body:
In `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 117-125), a slot is rejected only if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`. This has three defects:
1. If `slotStartTime` equals `overrideEnd`, `isAfter` is false, so a slot starting right when the override ends is treated as inside the override.
2. A slot that starts before `overrideStart` and ends after `overrideStart` (or starts before `overrideEnd` and ends after `overrideEnd`) is not rejected, allowing bookings that extend outside the override window.
3. If a user defines multiple date override ranges on the same day, `.find()` rejects the slot as soon as it is outside the first range without checking whether it fits inside another range on that day.

A slot is within an override range iff `slotStartTime >= overrideStart && slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

findings.title: Working hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end` and fails with split working hours
findings.body:
In `checkIfIsAvailable` (lines 138-151):
1. Line 142 computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` instead of using `slotEndTime`, so the event's duration is ignored and a slot starting before `workingHour.endTime` that extends past the end of working hours is still considered valid.
2. Using `workingHours.find(...)` to return `false` when a slot is outside *any* matching entry breaks schedules with multiple working-hour blocks on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), because a slot in the afternoon block will be outside the morning block, causing `.find` to match and `checkIfIsAvailable` to return `false`.
3. If `workingHours` has no entry for `slotStartTime.day()` at all, `.find` returns `undefined` and the slot is treated as available on a non-working day.

findings.title: Redundant `utcOffset` shift on `date.start`/`date.end` in `checkIfIsAvailable` double-shifts or un-shifts override times
findings.body: `getUserAvailability` already returns `dateOverrides` with `start` and `end` converted to the actual UTC instants of the override (e.g. a 14:00 IST override is returned as `08:30:00.000Z`). In `checkIfIsAvailable`, line 107 computes `utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0` and adds it to `date.start` and `date.end` before comparing against `slotStartTime` (which is in UTC). For an organizer in IST (+05:30), `utcOffset` is -330, shifting `08:30Z` to `03:00Z` and comparing that against UTC `slotStartTime` (`08:30Z`). In the added test (`getSchedule.test.ts`), `TestData.schedules.IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride` has `date` as a plain string rather than a `Date` object, so `getUserAvailability` skips it (`!!availability.date && availability.date instanceof Date`) and this code path in `checkIfIsAvailable` was never exercised by the test.
